items.plain: Stay calm and prepare to endure; being often troubled or tempted does not mean all is lost. You are human, not God or an angel. God lifts up mourners and those who know their weakness.
items.core_idea: Being human, you will falter; God raises the humble

items.plain: Do not argue about God's hidden judgments, such as why one person is favoured or afflicted and another raised up. These things are beyond human judgment, and no reasoning can search them out.
items.core_idea: God's judgments are beyond human reasoning

items.plain: Speaking to God: You are my only real comfort. I would rather be poor with You than rich without You, a wanderer with You than in heaven without You. Where You are is heaven.
items.core_idea: With God is heaven; without God is hell

items.plain: Speaking to God: I put all my hope and troubles in You, because everything else is weak. Friends, helpers, advisers, books, wealth and safe places are all useless unless You yourself help and comfort.
items.core_idea: Without God, no earthly help can truly help

items.plain: The Lord says: come to me, all of you who are worn out and weighed down, and I will give you rest.
items.core_idea: The Lord offers rest to the weary

items.plain: Trusting in Your goodness and mercy, Lord, I come to You as the sick come to a healer, the hungry to a fountain, the poor to a king, the creature to its Creator, the lonely to a gentle comforter.
items.core_idea: Coming to God as the needy come to help

items.plain: Speaking to God: give me Yourself and that is enough, since nothing else comforts. Without You I cannot exist, and without Your presence I have no strength to live.
items.core_idea: God alone is enough

items.plain: I toil, grieve, carry my sins and struggle with temptations, and no one can free me except You, Lord my Saviour. I entrust myself and all I have to You, to lead me to eternal life.
items.core_idea: In every burden, only God can deliver

items.plain: God says: all I ask is that you give yourself wholly to Me. Whatever else you give means nothing to Me, because I want you, not your gifts.
items.core_idea: God wants you, not your gifts

items.plain: Speaking to God: all I can do about my sins is confess, grieve and ask mercy. I mean to repent and make amends, and I put myself in Your hands. Treat me by Your kindness, not my wrongdoing.
items.core_idea: Confess, repent, and trust God's mercy

items.plain: A prayer: Lord, take from our hearts all suspicion, resentment, anger and quarrelling, and anything that harms love between people.
items.core_idea: Prayer to remove what harms love

items.plain: Follow the advice of wise people and put aside anxiety and over-scrupulous worry, because it blocks God's grace and destroys a devoted mind.
items.core_idea: Anxious scruples block grace and devotion

items.plain: Speaking to God: You are my witness that nothing and no one can comfort me or give me rest except You, whom I long to contemplate forever.
items.core_idea: Only God gives true rest

items.plain: If you feel no devotion and feel spiritually dry, keep praying hard. Keep groaning and knocking until you receive even a crumb or a drop of saving grace.
items.core_idea: In spiritual dryness, keep praying

items.plain: Speaking to God: truly You are my peacemaker. In You is perfect peace and rest; apart from You is toil, sorrow and endless misery.
items.core_idea: Peace is in God; misery apart from Him

items.plain: Seek devotion earnestly, wait for it patiently, receive and keep it humbly, and leave its timing to God. When you feel little devotion, be humble but not crushed. God often gives in a moment what He long withheld.
items.core_idea: Wait patiently for grace; God gives in time

items.plain: Speaking to the Lord: You know my weakness, my needs, and how often I am weighed down and tempted. I come to You for help and comfort, since You know all my secrets and alone can help me fully.
items.core_idea: Bringing one's weakness honestly to God

items.plain: Simple faith that skips difficult questioning and follows God's commandments is blessed. Many lost their devotion by probing deeper things. God asks faith and an honest life, not great intellect or insight into His mysteries.
items.core_idea: Faith and honest living matter more than intellect

items.plain: There is one God, whose name is truth: the Creator, without fear or hatred, undying, unborn, self-existent, known by the Guru's grace. Repeat His name. The True One was, is, and always will be.
items.core_idea: One true, eternal God

items.plain: No amount of thinking, silence, or worldly gain brings me to God, and no clever method helps. How can a person become true and tear away falsehood? Nanak says: by living according to God's will.
items.core_idea: God is reached by His will, not cleverness

items.plain: Everything comes by God's order: bodies, souls, greatness, high and low status, pain and pleasure, reward or endless rebirth. No one is outside it. Nanak says whoever understands God's order is free of ego.
items.core_idea: All is God's order; understanding it ends ego

items.plain: The state of someone who obeys God cannot be described, and whoever tries will regret it; no paper, pen or writer can capture it. God's name is so pure that whoever obeys Him feels its joy in their own heart.
items.core_idea: The joy of obeying God is beyond words

items.plain: As water cleans dirty hands and soap cleans clothes, God's name cleanses a mind stained by sin. No one becomes saint or sinner by calling themselves so; deeds are recorded, and each reaps what they sow.
items.core_idea: God's name cleanses; you reap what you sow

items.plain: Pilgrimage, austerity, mercy and charity may earn a little honour. But whoever hears, obeys and loves God in their heart is cleansed at the pilgrimage place within. All virtues are God's, none mine; without virtue there is no devotion.
items.core_idea: Inner love of God cleanses more than rituals

items.plain: Those who praise God still do not know Him fully, as rivers flow into the sea without knowing its size. Kings with mountains of wealth are not equal to a worm that keeps God in its heart.
items.core_idea: Remembering God outweighs all worldly wealth

items.plain: Wear contentment as your earrings, modesty and self-respect as your begging bag, and meditation as your holy ash. Make your body, which death will consume, your beggar's coat, and make faith your rule and your staff.
items.core_idea: Make inner virtues your true religious garb

items.plain: I have no power to speak or be silent, to ask or give, to live or die, to gain wealth, to meditate on God, or to escape the world. Before God, no one is stronger or weaker.
items.core_idea: Before God, no one has power of their own

fix.display_text: I have no strength to speak and no strength to be silent. I have no strength to ask and no strength to give; I have no strength to live and no strength to die; I have no strength to acquire empire or wealth, which produce a commotion in the heart. I have no strength to meditate on Thee or ponder on divine knowledge; I have no strength to find the way to escape from the world. He in whose arm there is strength may see what he can do. Nanak, no one is of superior or inferior strength before God.

items.plain: Make self-control your furnace, patience your goldsmith, understanding your anvil, divine knowledge your tools, fear of God your bellows, discipline your fire, and love your crucible; melt God's name in it. In such a true mint the Word is coined.
items.core_idea: Virtues are the forge where God's Word is made

items.plain: Air is our Guru, water our father, earth our mother. Our good and bad deeds will be read before the judge, bringing some near to God and some far. Those who dwelt on the Name will shine and free many.
items.core_idea: Deeds decide nearness to God; the Name brings freedom

items.plain: Just as hidden seed sprouts after years without rain, so good and evil, pains and pleasures, hates and loves, and all past deeds return, bearing bright or dark leaves, sweet or sour fruit.
items.core_idea: Past deeds return like seeds that sprout

items.plain: We are voices of the wandering wind, longing for rest and never finding it. Mortal life is like that wind: a moan, a sob, a storm. No one knows where life comes from or goes.
items.core_idea: Life is restless and changing like the wind

items.plain: Even if we held love and life so close that our breaths became one, time would still come between us and steal away my passion and your beauty, just as night quietly takes the rosy light from a mountain peak.
items.core_idea: Time steals even the closest love

items.plain: High and low, good and bad, all must die, and then, it is taught, begin again somewhere, somehow, who knows; and so again come the pain, the parting, and the funeral fire. Such is the human cycle.
items.core_idea: All die and the cycle of rebirth repeats

items.plain: Oh suffering world, I feel the vast agony of the earth and the emptiness of its joys. Pleasure ends in pain, youth in age, love in loss, life in death, and death in new lives on the same wheel.
items.core_idea: The world is caught in a wheel of suffering

items.plain: People froze until someone struck fire from flint, ate like wolves until someone sowed grain, and babbled until someone found speech and writing. Every good gift humanity has came from searching, struggle and loving sacrifice.
items.core_idea: Every human gift came from struggle and sacrifice

items.plain: Friend, love that clings to love for its own pleasures is false. I love these people more than my joy, even more than theirs, so I leave to save them and all beings, if utmost love can.
items.core_idea: True love is selfless, not clinging

items.plain: Speaking to ascetics: will you punish your body so hard for your soul's sake that it breaks down before the journey ends? Why wreck this house whose windows give the little light we search by?
items.core_idea: Don't destroy the body the spirit needs

items.plain: Palms reaching for the sky, what secret keeps you content from sprout to fruit? And you merry birds in the trees: none of you hate your life or think you must deny your needs to improve.
items.core_idea: Nature lives content without self-denial

items.plain: Yesterday the one you love died in your arms; today you know the whole world weeps with you. A grief that all hearts share grows lighter for each one.
items.core_idea: Shared grief grows lighter

items.plain: Pity and need make all beings family. There is no caste in blood or tears, which are alike in everyone, and no one is born marked by caste. Doing good makes a person noble; doing evil, base.
items.core_idea: Deeds, not birth, make a person noble

items.plain: A string pulled too tight snaps and the music is gone; a string too loose makes no sound. Tune us like a sitar, neither too low nor too high.
items.core_idea: Balance, not extremes, makes life work

items.plain: I believe good comes from good and evil from evil, everywhere: sweet fruit from healthy roots, hate from spite, friends from kindness, peace from patience. So after death, will the future not be as good as now?
items.core_idea: Good brings good, now and after death

items.plain: Like a climber on a summit looking back over every cliff, bog and ridge he crossed, the Buddha saw life's long chain of upward steps, from low levels to heights where the ten Virtues lead skyward.
items.core_idea: Life is a long upward climb toward virtue

items.plain: Through many lives I sought the builder of these sorrowful prisons of the senses. Now, builder, I know you; you will never build these walls of pain again. Delusion made your house, and it is broken. I go free.
items.core_idea: Seeing through delusion ends the cycle of suffering

items.plain: Evil adds to the debts you must pay; good frees and clears you. Avoid evil, do good, and rule over yourself. This is the Way.
items.core_idea: Shun evil, do good, master yourself

items.plain: A greater love bears patiently with a lesser one to lift it higher. Whoever has escaped bondage should not taunt those still bound. Be free so that you spread freedom through patience and gentle wisdom.
items.core_idea: Use your freedom to free others patiently

fix.display_text:
The greater beareth with the lesser love
So it may raise it unto easier heights.
Take heed that no man, being 'scaped from bonds,
Vexeth bound souls with boasts of liberty.
Free are ye rather that your freedom spread
By patient winning and sweet wisdom's skill.

items.plain: Do not pray; the darkness will not lighten and the silence cannot answer. Do not try to buy help from powerless gods with offerings. Freedom must be sought within; each person makes their own prison.
items.core_idea: Liberation is found within, not from gods

items.plain: Nothing lasts: good virtues wear away with time, and bad sins are cleansed by it.
items.core_idea: Time wears away both virtue and sin

items.plain: You are not bound: the heart of being is restful, and will is stronger than sorrow. I, the Buddha, who wept with the world, now rejoice in freedom. You suffer from yourselves; no one else holds you on the wheel.
items.core_idea: Your suffering comes from yourself; freedom is possible

items.plain: You reap what you sow: sesame grows sesame, corn grows corn. A person's fate grows from what they planted in past lives, good seed and weeds. If they pull the weeds and plant good seedlings, the harvest will be rich.
items.core_idea: You reap what you sow, across lives

items.plain: When gentle and just people die, the world grows richer, like a desert stream that sinks underground and rises again purer and wider.
items.core_idea: Good lives enrich the world after death

items.plain: Love is sweet, but the funeral fire will take the bodies that embrace; strength in war is fine, but vultures pick the bones of chiefs and kings.
items.core_idea: Love and power both end in death

items.plain: You cling to shadows and love dreams. You set a false self at the centre and build a world around it that only seems real, blind to the higher truth and the true life kept for whoever drops the false.
items.core_idea: A false self builds an unreal world

items.plain: Peace is overcoming self-love and craving, uprooting passion, and calming inner conflict. Let your love be eternal beauty, your glory self-mastery, your wealth service, duty, kindness, gentle speech and blameless days, riches that never fade.
items.core_idea: Peace is mastering self and craving

items.plain: Many paths lead up to the snowy peaks: the strong climb the steep road, the weak wind slowly with many rests. So the Eightfold Path to peace goes; the firm hurry, the feeble linger, but all arrive.
items.core_idea: All reach peace, fast or slow

items.plain: Wish well to every living thing, letting unkindness, greed and anger die, so that your lives become like gentle breezes passing by.
items.core_idea: Goodwill to all; let anger and greed die

items.plain: Guard your lips as if they were palace doors with a king inside; let every word that comes out be calm, kind and courteous.
items.core_idea: Guard your speech; keep it calm and kind

items.plain: Let each act undo a fault or help some good grow; let love show through good deeds like silver thread through crystal beads.
items.core_idea: Let every act show love

items.plain: I know love of spouse and child is dear, friends and pleasures sweet, and life's fears false though strong. Those who must, live such lives, but make your weakness a golden stair, rising through them to lovelier truths.
items.core_idea: Ordinary life can be a stair to truth

items.plain: Enter the Path! No sorrow is like hatred, no pain like passion, no deceit like the senses. Whoever overcomes even one cherished fault has come far.
items.core_idea: Overcoming one fault is real progress

items.plain: Do not bear false witness, slander, or lie; truthful speech comes from a pure heart.
items.core_idea: Truthful speech reflects inner purity

items.plain: Avoid drugs and drinks that cloud your mind; a clear mind and clean body need no intoxicant.
items.core_idea: A clear mind needs no intoxicants

items.plain: Don't scatter rice as offerings; instead offer loving thoughts and acts to everyone: parents, teachers, spouse and children, friends and all people, the smallest creatures, and the saints and dead above. That shuts out evil and keeps every direction safe.
items.core_idea: Offer love to all, not ritual offerings

items.plain: From Apollonius I learned free will, steady purpose and reliance on reason alone; to stay the same in pain, grief and illness; to be firm yet gentle; and to accept friends' favours without feeling humbled or ignoring them.
items.core_idea: Lessons in steadiness and reason from a teacher

items.plain: From Maximus I learned self-control and not being led astray, cheerfulness in every situation including illness, a blend of sweetness and dignity, and doing my tasks without complaint.
items.core_idea: Self-control, cheerfulness, and duty without complaint

items.plain: I owe it to the gods that I had good grandparents, parents, sister, teachers, companions, relatives and friends, almost everything good.
items.core_idea: Gratitude for the good people in my life

items.plain: Each morning, expect to meet meddling, ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful and envious people who don't know good from evil. They cannot harm you, and you cannot hate them, for they are your kin. We are made to work together.
items.core_idea: Expect difficult people; they are still your kin

items.plain: Remember how long you have put things off and wasted chances. Your time is limited, and if you don't use it to clear your mind, it will pass, you will pass, and it will never return.
items.core_idea: Your time is limited; stop putting things off

items.plain: Do each task with dignity, care, freedom and justice, setting other thoughts aside. You can, if you act each time as if it were your last, without carelessness, hypocrisy, self-love or discontent. A calm life needs little.
items.core_idea: Do each act as if it were your last

items.plain: Do outside events distract you? Take time to learn something good and stop being spun around. But avoid the opposite error too: people who wear themselves out with activity, with no aim for their actions and thoughts.
items.core_idea: Avoid distraction and aimless busyness alike

items.plain: People are rarely unhappy because they fail to notice what others are thinking, but those who don't watch their own minds are bound to be unhappy.
items.core_idea: Watch your own mind, not others'

items.plain: Since you could leave life this very moment, let every act and thought reflect that.
items.core_idea: Live as if you could die now

items.plain: Even if you lived thousands of years, you only ever lose the life you are living now. So the longest and shortest lives come to the same. No one can lose the past or future, because no one has them.
items.core_idea: Only the present moment can be lost

items.plain: Remember that everything depends on how you judge it.
items.core_idea: Everything is a matter of opinion

items.plain: Don't waste the rest of your life thinking about other people unless it serves some common good. Wondering what someone is doing, saying, thinking or plotting costs you other work and pulls you away from watching your own mind.
items.core_idea: Don't waste life wondering about others

items.plain: Be cheerful, and don't depend on outside help or on calm that others provide. A person must stand upright on their own, not be held up by others.
items.core_idea: Stand on your own, not propped up

items.plain: If you do the task in front of you by right reason, seriously, calmly and undistracted, keeping your divine part pure, expecting and fearing nothing, and speaking truthfully, you will live happily. No one can stop you.
items.core_idea: Do your present task well and be happy

items.plain: Stop drifting. You will never read the notes, histories and books you were saving for old age. Hurry toward your goal, drop empty hopes, and help yourself while you still can, if you care about yourself.
items.core_idea: Stop drifting; act for yourself now

items.plain: The ruling mind, following nature, easily adapts to whatever happens and turns obstacles into material for its purpose, like a strong fire that seizes what is thrown on it and burns higher because of it.
items.core_idea: A strong mind turns obstacles into fuel

items.plain: People seek retreats in the country, by the sea, in the mountains. But you can retreat into yourself whenever you choose, and nowhere is quieter than your own soul. Tranquility is a well-ordered mind; renew yourself there often.
items.core_idea: Retreat into your own mind for peace

items.plain: Death, like birth, is a mystery of nature: a coming together of elements and a coming apart into them. It is nothing to be ashamed of, since it is not against the nature or reason of a thinking being.
items.core_idea: Death is as natural as birth

items.plain: Drop your judgment, and the complaint "I have been harmed" goes with it. Drop that complaint, and the harm is gone.
items.core_idea: Harm lies in your judgment of it

items.plain: Don't see things the way the person who wrongs you sees them, or the way they want you to; see them as they truly are.
items.core_idea: See things as they are, not as wrongdoers would

items.plain: Keep two rules ready: do only what reason suggests for the good of others, and change your mind when someone corrects you, but only when convinced it is just or useful, not because it is pleasant or flattering.
items.core_idea: Act by reason; change your mind for good reasons

items.plain: Don't live as if you had ten thousand years. Death hangs over you. While you live and still can, be good.
items.core_idea: Death is near; be good now

items.plain: You avoid much trouble by not watching what your neighbour says, does or thinks, and attending only to whether your own actions are just and pure. Don't look around at others' bad conduct; run straight along your line.
items.core_idea: Mind your own conduct, not others'

items.plain: Whatever is beautiful is beautiful in itself; praise adds nothing and blame takes nothing away. Truly beautiful things, like truth, kindness or modesty, need nothing more. Is an emerald worse for not being praised?
items.core_idea: Beauty does not depend on praise

items.plain: Speaking to the Universe: whatever suits you suits me; nothing is too early or too late if it is on time for you. All your seasons bring is fruit to me, Nature: all comes from you and returns to you.
items.core_idea: Accept whatever nature brings, in its time

items.plain: Rather than merely doing few things, do what is necessary and what reason asks of a social being. Most of what we say and do is needless; cut it and gain peace. Ask: is this necessary? Cut needless thoughts too.
items.core_idea: Cut the unnecessary from acts and thoughts

items.plain: Love the craft you have learned, however humble, and be content with it. Live the rest of your life as one who has entrusted everything to the gods with his whole soul, being neither tyrant nor slave to anyone.
items.core_idea: Love your work; be no one's master or slave

items.plain: Even lasting fame is nothing. What deserves our serious effort is just one thing: fair thoughts, actions for the common good, honest words, and a willingness to accept everything that happens as necessary and natural.
items.core_idea: Fame is nothing; live justly and accept what comes

items.plain: Everything lasts only a day, both the one who remembers and the one who is remembered.
items.core_idea: All, remembered or remembering, is brief

items.plain: You will die soon, and you are still not simple, not calm, still fearing harm from outside, not kind to everyone, and not yet placing wisdom only in acting justly.
items.core_idea: Death is near and you still have work to do

items.plain: Time is like a fast-flowing river of events: as soon as something appears it is swept away, another takes its place, and that too is swept away.
items.core_idea: Time sweeps everything away like a river

items.plain: Everything that happens is as ordinary and familiar as roses in spring and fruit in summer, including illness, death, slander, betrayal, and whatever else pleases or upsets fools.
items.core_idea: Even hardship is as ordinary as the seasons

items.plain: If a god told you that you would die tomorrow or the day after, you would hardly care which, since the difference is tiny. So think it no great matter whether you die many years from now or tomorrow.
items.core_idea: A long life or short, the difference is small

items.plain: See how brief and worthless human things are: yesterday a speck, tomorrow ashes. Pass this short time in line with nature and end content, like a ripe olive falling, blessing nature and thanking the tree it grew on.
items.core_idea: Live by nature and depart content

items.plain: Be like a headland that the waves keep crashing against: it stands firm and calms the raging water around it.
items.core_idea: Stand firm like a rock against waves

items.plain: Don't say "I'm unhappy because this happened." Say "I'm fortunate, because though this happened I stay free from pain, not crushed by the present or afraid of the future." It could happen to anyone, but not everyone would stay untroubled.
items.core_idea: Bearing misfortune well is good fortune

items.plain: When you don't want to get up in the morning, remember: I am rising to do a human being's work. Why resent doing what I exist for? Was I made to lie under the blankets and keep warm?
items.core_idea: You were made for work, not for bed

items.plain: How easy it is to push away and wipe out every troubling or unsuitable impression, and at once be completely calm.
items.core_idea: You can dismiss troubling thoughts and be calm

items.plain: Treat every word and act that accords with nature as fitting for you, and don't be put off by others' blame. If something is good to do or say, do it. Ignore others' ways; follow your own and nature's.
items.core_idea: Do what is right; ignore others' blame

items.plain: You say people can't admire your cleverness. Fine, but you can show qualities fully in your power: sincerity, seriousness, endurance, contentment, kindness, frankness, simplicity, generosity of spirit. No natural lack excuses you, yet you choose to fall short.
items.core_idea: Show the virtues already within your power

fix.display_text: Thou sayest, Men cannot admire the sharpness of thy wits.⁠—Be it so: but there are many other things of which thou canst not say, I am not formed for them by nature. Show those qualities then which are altogether in thy power, sincerity, gravity, endurance of labour, aversion to pleasure, contentment with thy portion and with few things, benevolence, frankness, no love of superfluity, freedom from trifling, magnanimity. Dost thou not see how many qualities thou art immediately able to exhibit, in which there is no excuse of natural incapacity and unfitness, and yet thou still remainest voluntarily below the mark?

items.plain: Some who do a good turn count it as a favour owed; others silently treat the person as in their debt. A third kind hardly notices, like a vine that bears grapes, asks nothing, and goes on bearing.
items.core_idea: Do good without seeking credit, like a vine

items.plain: Don't be disgusted or discouraged when you fail to live by right principles. Come back, be content if most of what you do fits human nature, and treat philosophy not as a harsh master but as a soothing remedy.
items.core_idea: When you fail, return gently and keep going

items.plain: Your mind takes on the character of your habitual thoughts, because the soul is dyed by them. So dye it with thoughts like this: wherever a person can live, they can also live well.
items.core_idea: Your thoughts shape the character of your mind

items.plain: Nothing happens to anyone that they are not made by nature to bear. Others face the same things and stay firm, from ignorance or wanting to look brave. It is shameful that ignorance and vanity should outdo wisdom.
items.core_idea: You are made to bear what happens to you

items.plain: Things themselves cannot touch, enter or move the soul at all. The soul moves itself, and whatever judgments it chooses to make shape how things appear to it.
items.core_idea: Only your judgments move your soul

items.plain: I must do good to people and bear with them. But when they block my proper actions, they are as neutral as sun or wind. They can hinder my acts, not my mind, which turns obstacles into help.
items.core_idea: The mind turns obstacles into help

items.plain: Think often how quickly everything passes: all flows like a river, hardly anything stands still, and the endless past and future swallow everything. Isn't it foolish, then, to be puffed up or tormented by things that trouble you so briefly?
items.core_idea: All passes quickly; don't be tormented by it

items.plain: Does someone wrong me? That's their concern; they have their own character and actions. I have what universal nature wants me to have now, and I do what my nature wants me to do now.
items.core_idea: Others' wrongs are their concern

items.plain: Are you angry at someone's body odour or bad breath? Anger does no good; it comes naturally. He could see his fault? You have reason too: use it to show him his error. If he listens, anger is needless.
items.core_idea: Correct others with reason, not anger

fix.display_text: Art thou angry with him whose armpits stink? Art thou angry with him whose mouth smells foul? What good will this anger do thee? He has such a mouth, he has such armpits: it is necessary that such an emanation must come from such things⁠—but the man has reason, it will be said, and he is able, if he takes pain, to discover wherein he offends⁠—I wish thee well of thy discovery. Well then, and thou hast reason: by thy rational faculty stir up his rational faculty; show him his error, admonish him. For if he listens, thou wilt cure him, and there is no need of anger.

items.plain: Remember how much you have endured; that your life's story is complete and your service done; how many beautiful things you have seen, how many pleasures and pains you have spurned, and how kind you have been to ill-minded people.
items.core_idea: Recall all you have endured and done well

items.plain: Very soon you will be ashes or bones, a name or not even that, and a name is only an echo. What life prizes is empty and petty, like puppies biting each other or children quarrelling, laughing, then crying.
items.core_idea: What we prize in life is empty and brief

items.plain: You can live in a steady flow of happiness if you go the right way and think and act rightly.
items.core_idea: Right thought and action bring steady happiness

items.plain: If you are doing your duty, let it not matter whether you are cold or warm, tired or rested, criticised or praised, dying or doing something else. Dying is also an act of life; there too, just do it well.
items.core_idea: Do your duty whatever your condition, even dying

items.plain: The best revenge is not to become like the person who wronged you.
items.core_idea: The best revenge is not to be like them

items.plain: When circumstances force you to lose your composure, return to yourself quickly and don't stay out of tune longer than you must. The more often you return to your inner harmony, the better you will master it.
items.core_idea: Return quickly to inner harmony when shaken

items.plain: How strange people are: they won't praise those living alongside them, yet they badly want praise from future people they will never see. That is like being upset that people who lived before you didn't praise you.
items.core_idea: Craving posthumous praise is absurd

items.plain: If something is hard for you, don't assume it is impossible for people. If it is possible for people and fits human nature, believe you can achieve it too.
items.core_idea: What others can do, you can do too

items.plain: In the gym, if a sparring partner scratches you or butts your head, you don't get upset or call him treacherous; you quietly keep out of his way. Do the same in life: overlook much, step aside, hold no hatred.
items.core_idea: Overlook offences; step aside without hatred

items.plain: If anyone can show me that I think or act wrongly, I will gladly change, because I seek the truth, and truth never harmed anyone. The one harmed is whoever stays in error and ignorance.
items.core_idea: Gladly accept correction; truth harms no one

items.plain: Asked to spell a name, you wouldn't shout each letter or get angry back at angry listeners; you'd calmly go letter by letter. So every duty has parts. Attend to them and, without anger at angry people, finish the task.
items.core_idea: Calmly finish your duty, step by step

items.plain: How cruel to stop people pursuing what seems good to them, yet you do so when angry at their wrongdoing, since they pursue what they think is good for them. They are mistaken? Then teach them, without anger.
items.core_idea: Teach wrongdoers instead of being angry

items.plain: It is shameful for your soul to give up in this life while your body is still holding on.
items.core_idea: Don't let your spirit quit before your body

items.plain: Come back to your senses and wake yourself up. Just as on waking you see that only dreams troubled you, now look at the things around you the same way you looked at those dreams.
items.core_idea: See waking troubles as you see dreams

items.plain: Adapt yourself to the circumstances your life has given you, and love the people you have been placed among, truly and sincerely.
items.core_idea: Accept your lot and love those around you

items.plain: If you think things outside your control are good or bad for you, misfortune or loss will make you blame the gods and hate people. Count only what is in your power as good or bad, and that blame disappears.
items.core_idea: Judge only what you control as good or bad

items.plain: One thing here is worth a great deal: to live in truth and justice, with goodwill even toward liars and unjust people.
items.core_idea: Live truly and justly, kind even to the unjust

items.plain: To cheer yourself up, think of the good qualities of the people around you: one's energy, another's modesty, a third's generosity. Nothing delights like seeing virtue in those we live with, so keep it in mind.
items.core_idea: Delight in the virtues of those around you

items.plain: You aren't unhappy that you weigh only so much and not three hundred pounds. So don't be unhappy that you will live only so many years and no more; be content with your time as you are with your size.
items.core_idea: Be content with your lifespan

items.plain: We have the power to form no opinion about a thing and so stay undisturbed, because things themselves cannot force our judgments.
items.core_idea: Things can't force your judgments

items.plain: Train yourself to listen closely to what others say, and as far as possible, enter into the speaker's mind.
items.core_idea: Listen closely and understand the speaker

items.plain: To someone with jaundice honey tastes bitter; someone bitten by a mad dog fears water; children love a ball. So why am I angry? Does a false belief have less power over someone than bile or poison?
items.core_idea: People's errors work like illness; why be angry

items.plain: Your principles die only if the thoughts behind them go out, and you can keep fanning those into flame. Outside things have no hold on your mind. You can recover your life by seeing things again as you once did.
items.core_idea: Rekindle your principles to recover your life

items.plain: Is my understanding enough for this? If so, I use it as nature's tool. If not, I step aside for someone abler, or do my best with help. Whatever I do, alone or with others, should serve the common good.
items.core_idea: Do what you can, with help, for the common good

items.plain: How many once famous people are now forgotten, and how many who praised the famous are long dead.
items.core_idea: Fame and its admirers both fade

items.plain: Don't be ashamed to accept help. Your job is to do your duty, like a soldier storming a city wall. If you are lame and can't climb the wall alone, but can with someone's help, what then?
items.core_idea: Don't be ashamed to accept help

items.plain: Don't let the future trouble you. If you must face it, you will meet it with the same reason you use now for the present.
items.core_idea: Face the future with the reason you have now

items.plain: Let whatever happens fall on the parts that can feel it; they may complain if they like. But I am not harmed unless I judge what happened to be bad, and it is in my power not to judge so.
items.core_idea: No harm unless you judge it harm

items.plain: Whatever anyone does or says, I must be good, as gold or an emerald might say. Whatever anyone does or says, I must be an emerald and keep my colour.
items.core_idea: Stay good whatever others do

items.plain: Happiness means a good inner spirit. So, imagination, what are you doing here? Go away, as you came; I don't want you. You came in your old habitual way. I'm not angry with you; just go.
items.core_idea: Calmly dismiss unwanted imaginings

items.plain: Are you afraid of change? Nothing happens without it, and nothing suits nature better. You can't have a hot bath unless wood changes, or be fed unless food changes. Your own change is just as natural and necessary.
items.core_idea: Change is natural and necessary, including yours

items.plain: Soon you will forget everything, and soon everyone will forget you.
items.core_idea: All forgetting and being forgotten is near

items.plain: It is distinctly human to love even wrongdoers. You can, if you remember they are your kin, that they err from ignorance and not on purpose, that you will both soon die, and that they have not harmed your mind.
items.core_idea: Love wrongdoers; they cannot harm your mind

items.plain: When someone wrongs you, consider what they believed was good or bad. Then you will pity them, not be angry. If you share that belief, forgive them; if not, you will more easily be kind to someone mistaken.
items.core_idea: Understand a wrongdoer's beliefs, then forgive

items.plain: Think less of what you lack than of what you have. Pick the best of it and imagine how eagerly you would seek it if you didn't have it. But don't grow so attached that losing it would upset you.
items.core_idea: Value what you have without clinging

items.plain: Wipe out imaginings. Stop being pulled like a puppet. Stay in the present. Understand what happens to you and others. Separate cause from matter. Think of your last hour. Leave a wrong where it was done.
items.core_idea: Stay present; leave wrongs where they happened

items.plain: On pain: unbearable pain ends us, and lasting pain is bearable. The mind keeps its calm by withdrawing into itself, and its ruling part is not made worse. Let the parts hurt by pain speak for themselves if they can.
items.core_idea: Pain is bearable; the mind stays whole

items.plain: On fame: look at the minds of people who chase it, what they avoid and what they pursue. And remember that as new sand piles over old sand, so in life earlier events are quickly buried by later ones.
items.core_idea: Fame is soon buried like sand

items.plain: It is not right to be upset with things, because they don't care about it at all.
items.core_idea: Things don't care about your anger

items.plain: Everywhere and always, you can reverently accept your present situation, treat the people around you justly, and carefully examine your present thoughts so that nothing slips in unchecked.
items.core_idea: Accept the present, act justly, watch your thoughts

items.plain: Think of yourself as already dead, your life finished up to now, and live the rest you are given in line with nature.
items.core_idea: Live the remaining time as a bonus, by nature

items.plain: Look within. The source of good is inside you, and it will keep bubbling up if you keep digging.
items.core_idea: The source of good is within you

items.plain: Living well is more like wrestling than dancing: you must stand ready and steady to meet sudden, unexpected attacks.
items.core_idea: Life demands readiness, like wrestling

items.plain: Keep looking at whose approval you want and what principles guide them. Then you won't blame those who offend unintentionally, and you won't crave their approval once you see where their opinions and desires come from.
items.core_idea: Examine whose approval you seek

items.plain: The philosopher says every soul is deprived of truth against its will, and so likewise of justice, self-control, kindness and the rest. Keep this in mind constantly, and you will be gentler with everyone.
items.core_idea: No one errs willingly; be gentle with all

items.plain: Pain is no disgrace and does not harm your mind. As Epicurus said, pain is neither unbearable nor endless if you recall its limits and add nothing to it. Drowsiness, heat and lost appetite are pain too.
items.core_idea: Pain has limits; don't add to it

items.plain: Nature lets you govern what is yours; you can be godlike yet known to no one. Little is needed for a happy life. If you've abandoned hope of great learning, still be free, modest, sociable and obedient to God.
items.core_idea: Little is needed to live well and nobly

items.plain: Moral perfection is living each day as your last, without frantic excitement, laziness or pretence.
items.core_idea: Live each day as the last, calmly and honestly
